# railway_project (Resource)

A Railway project. Railway creates the project's first environment with it; put resources in it through `default_environment_id`, or add more with `railway_environment`. Creating a project needs an account or workspace token. Destroying it deletes everything in it, so consider `prevent_destroy`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "railway_project" "app" {
  name                     = "app"
  description              = "Managed by Terraform"
  default_environment_name = "production"

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

resource "railway_environment" "staging" {
  project_id = railway_project.app.id
  name       = "staging"
}

resource "railway_service" "web" {
  for_each = {
    production = railway_project.app.default_environment_id
    staging    = railway_environment.staging.id
  }
  environment_id = each.value
  name           = "web"
  source         = { image = { image = "traefik/whoami:v1.10" } }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Project name.

### Optional

- `default_environment_name` (String) Name of the environment Railway creates with the project. Railway names it `production` when unset. Changing it renames the environment.
- `description` (String) Project description.
- `is_public` (Boolean) Whether anyone can view the project.
- `pr_deploys` (Boolean) Whether Railway creates an environment for each pull request.
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace that owns the project. Defaults to the token's workspace. Changing it replaces the project.

### Read-Only

- `default_environment_id` (String) ID of the environment Railway created with the project.
- `id` (String) Project ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project_id>
terraform import railway_project.app 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
